unharnessed.meaning: Every point and every rejected option survives, with the reasons; the gals answer and all four examples are kept. "rule of life: sometimes people don't whinge about stuff they bloody well should" matches.
unharnessed.sense: Fits throughout: "a mob of blokes", "taking the piss" for mockery, "get anyone's back up" for offend, "might get a funny look" for a strange reaction.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural: "switched the light on", "not likely to be a drama", "rock up to a couple of women", "mightn't be keen on it".
unharnessed.register: A solid level-3 retelling, lighter than a level-5 pub yarn: much is close paraphrase ("too formal, or fake respect", "too matter-of-fact"). Vulgarity "dodgy as fuck" sits within uncle-bob.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the earnest, slightly self-deprecating forum voice and the helpful-answer tone; "watch yourself" fits the caution.
unharnessed.flow: Reads cleanly: "But rock up to a couple of women on a street corner and say this, and you might get a funny look".
unharnessed.variety: Varied, though "mob" three times and "casual" doubles for both informal and colloquial.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the question and its answer, list structure intact.

yarn.meaning: All points kept, but some are tweaked: "y'all" becomes "the Southern Yank one, 'you all' squashed into a single word", examples get "ute" and "supermarket", and condescending becomes "bein' a smart-arse".
yarn.sense: "bein' a smart-arse about it" is not condescending, and "dudes: too slack" uses slack (lazy/unfair) for informal; otherwise apt ("wouldn't have a bar of", "takin' the mickey").
yarn.authenticity: Largely natural ("Not a bugger ever whinged", "bland as", "dodgy as", "Righto"), with a few off notes: "coves" is dated, "folks" is American.
yarn.register: A full level-5 yarn: dropped g's, "a table full of suits", "too much like a police report"; swearing "smart-arse", "bloody", "bugger" within level 2.
yarn.tone: Keeps the earnest-but-casual asker and helpful answerer, a touch more larrikin than the original ("Okay, so.").
yarn.flow: Mostly smooth; the apostrophes get heavy ("prob'ly readin' somethin'") and the y'all line is clunky.
yarn.variety: Wide range: "chuck", "coves", "punters", "rapt", "bland as", "had a yarn", "brand-spankin'-new ute".
yarn.essence: Plainly the same Q&A, list and examples in place, retold in a pub voice.

engine.meaning: Swaps the word under discussion: "what's a feminine version of 'blokes'?", "'Blokes' can be used in English as gender neutral", "sheilas and gentlemen" and "coves, mate". The reader gets a different, false question.
engine.sense: "sheilas and gentlemen" for ladies and gentlemen, "young fellas" for boys, "battlers" for people, "punters" for a group: many wrong senses.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian bolt-ons: "Strewth", "Stone the crows", "Crikey", "Fair fuckin' dinkum", "Fuck me dead", "ya mug"; US "patronizing" left in.
engine.register: Lots of exclamations but the body is untranslated ("I commonly use the word 'blokes' to refer to a group of males colloquially"); not a real level-5 retelling.
engine.tone: The polite enquiry becomes rude at random: "ya mug", "Fuck me dead".
engine.flow: Broken joins: "Stone the crows, so, some that I wouldn't consider", "What might be a female gendered or non-gendered version of 'coves'? Dunno."
engine.variety: Exclamation tics and "sheilas"/"coves" over and over.
engine.essence: The question about "guys" is gone; it is no longer about that word.

unharnessed.original: What is a feminine version of 'guys'?
unharnessed.why: "sheila" as an adjective for feminine is a bit odd, though readable.
"casual" reused for colloquial, informal and the guys/gals variant; a touch flat for level 5.
Much of the text is close paraphrase rather than a level-5 yarn.

yarn.why: Smart-arse means cheeky or know-all, not condescending.
Slack in Aussie means lazy or unfair, not informal.

yarn.quote: the Southern Yank one, "you all" squashed into a single word
yarn.why: Drops the actual word under discussion for a description.
Edits the quoted example; "brand-spankin'-new" is added detail.

engine.quote: Strewth, what's a feminine version of 'blokes'?
engine.original: What is a feminine version of 'guys'?
engine.why: Replaces the word the whole post is about.

engine.quote: “Blokes” can be used in English as gender neutral
engine.original: “Guys” can be used in English as gender neutral
engine.why: False claim; blokes is not gender neutral.
Garbles the phrase the answer compares to.
Insult added to an example sentence.
Bolted-on oath with no anchor in the original.

summaries.unharnessed: Clean, accurate and natural, but pitched nearer level 3 than the level-5 brief.
summaries.yarn: The most fully Aussie and lively retelling, with a couple of terms that miss the sense.
summaries.engine: A word-swap mess that changes the subject of the question and bolts on oaths.
